Water | Representative Susie Lee Skip to main content Water Nevada is a national leader when it comes to protecting our water supply, but there’s more work to be done as we face the ongoing effects of the American West’s worst drought in 12 centuries. As Vice-Chair of the bipartisan Colorado River Caucus, I am dedicated to finding solutions that will improve on our successful practices, keep more water in Lake Mead, and protect our water supply for generations to come. Investing in Water Infrastructure Last Congress, my Large-Scale Water Recycling Project Investment Act was signed into law as part of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law , along with more than $400 million to improve Nevada’s water infrastructure. In 2023, I secured more than $122 million for local water projects, including the Las Vegas Wash and Lake Mead. And in 2024, I helped secure another $4 million for the Lake Mead/Las Vegas Wash Program.  Managing Water Data This Congress, I’ve introduced bipartisan legislation to close the biggest data gap in water management to get critical water use data in the hands of water managers, farmers, ranchers, and decision-makers for improved water management and stewardship – because you can't manage what you can't measure. The Colorado River I led a bipartisan group of U.S. Representatives calling on the Biden Administration to take federal action to safeguard the Colorado River System after a series of missed deadlines. This call to action helped build the momentum necessary for the Colorado River Basin states to reach a historic agreement to voluntarily conserve 3 million additional acre-feet of water over the next three years. The Las Vegas Wash and Lake Mead The Las Vegas Wash carries more than 200 million gallons of water to Lake Mead every day and allows southern Nevada to recycle nearly every drop of water it uses indoors. I’ve introduced legislation to raise the funding cap of the federal Las Vegas Wash program – and joined with the Commissioner of the Bureau of Reclamation in 2023 to announce $20 million in Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funding to protect and restore the Wash. Housing | Representative Susie Lee Skip to main content Housing I know that affordable housing isn’t just a priority in southern Nevada — it’s a necessity. I hear from folks who are struggling to keep a roof over their head: working parents trying to raise a family, veterans struggling to transition back to civilian life, and seniors who deserve better after retiring from a long career. All of these folks deserve housing that is safe, stable, and affordable. That’s why housing is one of my top priorities in Congress and what I’ve prioritized from my position on the House Appropriations Committee, which is in charge of distributing federal funds across the country. Cracking Down on Corporate Price Gouging Southern Nevada homes should be owned by southern Nevadans — not by corporate landlords or cash rich investors who outbid working families and jack up prices. Sadly, local reporting has uncovered that as many as 15% of single family homes in Las Vegas are owned by these investors, with the largest corporate landlord in Clark County owning over 3,700 homes — more than double what they owned in 2019. Recent studies even suggest that corporate entities could own up to 40% of homes nationwide by 2030. Meanwhile, Nevada has only 14 available affordable homes per 100 low-income households and lacks approximately 80,000 affordable housing units to meet the local demand. This is what an affordable housing crisis looks like. That’s why I’m a proud supporter of the Housing Oversight and Mitigating Exploitation (HOME) Act , which would make it illegal to rent or sell a unit at an unreasonable price during an emergency like the one we currently face. It also directs the Department of Housing and Urban Development to investigate price manipulation and price gouging by these corporate investors. From Big Pharma to Big Oil, I’m standing up to massive corporations that want to squeeze hardworking families and seniors. Housing is no different. I’ll keep fighting to lower your costs because I represent southern Nevadans — not special interests. Health Care | Representative Susie Lee Skip to main content Health Care When my father was 56, he lost his job and my parents were unable to afford health insurance. Then, one month before my mother qualified for Medicare, she suffered a major heart attack. We almost lost our home trying to pay off the hospital bills. I know what it’s like to struggle without access to medical care because I lived it while growing up in a working-class family of ten, and I know every American has a story like mine. In Congress, I’m fighting to keep families healthy and ensure access to high-quality care — no matter where you live — at the lowest possible cost. Holding Big Pharma Accountable Last Congress, I stood up to Big Pharma and passed legislation to lower costs for seniors by capping the cost of insulin at $35 a month, capping out of pocket costs at $2,000 a year, and lowering prescription drug prices across the board. Now, I’m continuing that fight to lower costs and make drug prices more transparent so families can make better decisions and see their lower costs in real time. Expanding Telehealth and Rural Health Care Access For too many people who live in underserved and rural areas, it is difficult to physically get to a doctor's office. But with the enactment of my MOBILE Health Care Act , Federally Qualified Health Centers can now acquire and dispatch more mobile clinics, which will help bring essential health care to people where they are. I’m continuing this work toward more accessible care by making sure telehealth specialists can reach every community across southern Nevada.  Providing Mental Health Resources Whether you’re a student struggling in school or a veteran transitioning back to civilian life, I’m fighting to get folks the resources and care they need. My bipartisan TREAT Youth Act would protect and support youth and families struggling with substance abuse by reauthorizing a program to improve youth awareness of risks associated with fentanyl and opioids, increase access to relevant medications, and train health care providers on best practices for supporting youth suffering from substance abuse. Immigration & Border Security | Representative Susie Lee Skip to main content Immigration & Border Security Our immigration system and southern border have been broken for decades, jeopardizing our national security and economy. That’s why I supported the Senate’s tough and fair bipartisan border security deal that was negotiated by both parties and have called on House Republican leadership to let us vote on it. I also worked with Republicans and Democrats to craft a bipartisan proposal to hire 1,500 new border patrol agents and crack down on fentanyl entering the U.S. I’m a cosponsor of the bipartisan Dignity Act and a staunch advocate for comprehensive, bipartisan immigration reform that will secure our borders and create a system that is fast, fair, and final for anyone seeking a better life and to contribute to our economy. It’s critical that we protect our border, create a path to citizenship, and process asylum claims more efficiently, so those who are fleeing violence and persecution can come here to live, work, pay taxes, and strengthen our economy. We need to keep people safe, boost our economy, and preserve the American Dream. Protecting Our Border As a member of the Democrats for Border Security Task Force , I’m working to ensure that our law enforcement has all the tools and resources they need to protect our border and go after human and drug traffickers. I’m proud to have voted to increase funding for border patrol personnel and fentanyl scanning technology. I’m fighting to make sure our border is fully funded in smart and efficient ways. Creating a Path to Citizenship Every day, I have conversations with House Republicans and just about all of them agree we need to protect our border and process asylum claims more efficiently, so those who are fleeing violence and persecution can come here to live, work, pay taxes, and strengthen our economy. I have helped craft a framework to protect our border, support our economy, and provide a pathway to citizenship. But unfortunately, the far-right leadership on the other side of the aisle has decided to continue to use our immigration system as a political football.  Boosting Our Economy and Wo

Economy, Jobs, & Small Businesses | Representative Susie Lee Skip to main content Economy, Jobs, & Small Businesses My father served our country overseas and came home to a steel plant in Ohio, where he raised me and my seven siblings in a working-class family of ten. When I was eight years old, I started my own paper route to help pitch in because we had to stretch every dollar we had. I know the value of hard work and I know southern Nevadans do too. That’s why lowering costs and expanding economic opportunity are one of my top priorities in Congress. So much of my work, particularly through annual funding bills on the House Appropriations Committee, is centered around giving hard working families the tools to succeed while bringing federal dollars back to southern Nevada. That means making it easier to support a family, creating good-paying jobs, and building infrastructure to connect our communities. It also means working to diversify our economy by supporting local small businesses, investing in domestic manufacturing, and developing our workforce. Lowering Costs Thanks to the Inflation Reduction Act that I helped pass , seniors on Medicare now have lower prescription drugs, a $35 monthly cap on insulin, and a $2,000 monthly cap on out-of-pocket costs – and I’ll keep fighting to make this life-changing support available to more Americans. I’m also fighting to strengthen our supply chains, invest in domestic manufacturing, build more affordable housing, and make it easier to access cost-efficient renewable energy options for your home. Bringing Jobs to Southern Nevada and Diversifying Our Economy I’m fighting every day to grow and diversify our local economy by bringing new companies and good-paying jobs to our community. The Inflation Reduction Act has already helped companies expand in southern Nevada and will continue to do so as we make clear to employers that we are open for business and ready to invest. From world-renowned technological innovation to hands-on manufacturing , southern Nevada is quickly becoming a hub for economic opportunity in the 21st century. Women's Rights | Representative Susie Lee Skip to main content Women's Rights I was first elected to Congress alongside a historic wave of female lawmakers across the country. Today, I’m honoring that history by continuing to fight for our most fundamental rights, representation, and equity in southern Nevada and beyond. I also know that since the fall of Roe v. Wade, which protected a woman’s right to choose nationwide, women’s freedoms are under attack like never before. Anti-choice extremists have introduced legislation for a national abortion ban and now they’re threatening access to IVF and contraception. As someone who suffered with infertility for years, I have my two beautiful children because of IVF. I understand how tough reproductive health care decisions can be. That’s how I know that no politician should get between a woman and her doctor. Protecting A Woman’s Freedom to Make Private Health Care Decisions Without the protections of Roe v. Wade, even states like Nevada live under threat of a national abortion ban and reproductive freedom is under constant threat. That’s why I’m championing legislation to help women who are fleeing anti-choice states to connect with the care providers they need, protecting access to birth control, and codifying the protections of Roe v. Wade . I won’t rest until every woman has the freedom to make private reproductive and health care decisions about her own body. Defending the Right to Start or Grow a Family Through IVF In vitro fertilization (IVF) is how millions of parents have started or grown their family. I know how difficult this process can be because IVF gave me my family. The truth is that infertility is an illness – one that I struggled with for a long time – but IVF is the treatment. That’s why I support the Access to Family Building Act , which would establish a legal right to IVF and other assisted reproductive services for families just like mine. Demanding Equal Pay for Equal Work Generations of women have fought for their rights in the workplace and finally closing the wage gap that has been present for all of our history is critical. Infrastructure | Representative Susie Lee Skip to main content Infrastructure I helped negotiate and pass the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to rebuild our roads and bridges, invest in climate resiliency, deliver clean drinking water, improve our airports, expand broadband access, develop more mass transit options, and create millions of jobs. This legislation is the largest infrastructure package in a generation and is already delivering much needed investments to southern Nevada. Reducing Traffic, Improving Traffic Safety It’s no secret that southern Nevadans spend a lot of time in their car. To make sure that time is efficient and safe, I’ve fought to bring federal dollars back to southern Nevada to update the Henderson Interchange and fund initiatives to make our streets safer for cars and pedestrians. Recently, I secured a $3.3 million investment to cut down on car crashes and boost pedestrian safety in some of our community’s most dangerous intersections. I’ve also worked alongside local and federal safety agencies to promote safe driving practices. The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law I helped negotiate and pass also made one of southern Nevada’s most transformative projects to date possible: Brightline West, our nation’s first high-speed rail system. Brightline West will make travel between Las Vegas and southern California twice as fast as by car and is projected to remove 3 million cars from the I-15 annually, create thousands of good-paying union jobs, boost the local economy, and reduce more than 400,000 tons of carbon emissions. That means less traffic, cleaner air, and more travelers to support southern Nevada’s 24/7 economy and small businesses.  Expanding Affordable Broadband Access Nevada lags behind much of the nation in access to high-speed internet, which is why I’ve fought to invest federal dollars in broadband services. But I’m also working to make sure Nevada gets its fair share of that funding to protect educational opportunities, access to health care, and economic growth for years to come. Appropriations | Representative Susie Lee Skip to main content Appropriations As southern Nevada’s voice on the House Appropriations Committee, which is responsible for distributing federal funds across the nation, my top priority is returning these dollars to our community. In addition to annual appropriations bills, I have also been able to return nearly $4 billion to Nevada taxpayers through local grants and federal investments in Nevada’s infrastructure, law enforcement, transportation, mental health services, housing, public lands and more. As a member of the subcommittees on Energy & Water as well as Military Construction & Veterans Affairs, I'm working to secure important investments for southern Nevada to support our veterans and military families, strengthen drought prevention efforts in the West, and continue to build a diverse, clean, and efficient energy economy that unleashes our state’s energy potential while lowering costs and protecting our public lands.
